newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Springer sees higher '96 profit.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Springer sees higher '96 profit.

text.p: Germany's largest newspaper publisher Springer Verlag AG said on Wednesday it expects operating profits to be unchanged in 1996 but that after-tax earnings would be higher than the previous year.

Springer said sales in the first ten months of the year grew 3.3 percent to 3.575 billion marks. Of the total sales of publications rose four percent to 1.572 billion marks and advertising revenue rose one percent to 1.518 billion.

Costs were also on the rise in the first ten months of the year. Paper costs were up by 90 million marks and start-up losses for new publications and online activities totalled around 40 million marks.
"Despite the higher costs, the management board expects nearly unchanged operating profit and net profit above the levels of the previous year," the company said in a statement.
In 1995 operating profit was 330 million marks and net income was 142 million marks. Liquidity was currently 725 million marks, Spinger said.
It said personnel costs to the end of October, including restructuring charges, rose three percent to 1.108 billion marks. The workforce fell by 263 to 12,129 employees.
